This is important because, back in the day, when you took a people into slavery, you killed all of the politicians, priests, and artisans. This effectively destroyed the culture and made it impossible for the slaves to revolt, escape, and rebuild themselves. After spending more than a few years in captivity, the Babylons (remember Nebuchadnezzar?) let them go. Tasked with rebuilding their culture, they rewrote the Pentateuch... we'd call them the first 5 books of the Old Testament. The problem is that no one really remembered what was in them. So they had help from the Babylonian scholars and <poof>... out pops a collection of texts that basically parallel the Enuma Elish, the Babylonian's holy texts. For example, seven days of creation for the seven clay tablets (and each creation matching the theme of each tablet), Tiamat, Leviathan, etc ad naseum.
